Subject: Re: POC trial environment options & next steps

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed plan so we have shared expectations before we kick off: 

Success criteria (what AcmeAI told us):
- 95th percentile latency < 200ms for our customer-facing summarization flow (seq len ~512)
- Sustained throughput ~30 reqs/sec for batch scoring during peak windows
- Model output quality on our eval set: Rouge-L >= 0.72 (we'll share the test prompts)
- No sensitive customer data stored beyond retention window (30 days)

Evaluation plan / timeline (proposed 3 weeks):
1) Week 0 (prep, target start 2027-02-28): contract/SOW + environment choice + access
2) Week 1 (env setup & connectivity): sandbox provision, ingest sample dataset, run smoke tests
3) Week 2 (workload runs): run latency/throughput benchmark scenarios + quality evals
4) Week 3 (tuning & wrap): iterate on batching/quantization settings, finalize findings & next steps

Environment options (pros/cons):
- Hosted (fastest): Redwood-hosted trial, quickest to stand up (same-day to 48h). Good for validating quality/latency on representative traffic. Limited data retention controls compared to private options.
- Dedicated sandbox (reserved): Dedicated GPU pool for predictable throughput, typical lead time ~1 week, good if you need consistent performance for benchmarking.
- VPC trial (private control plane): Best for compliance/data-retention (KMS, VPC peering). Lead time ~2-3 weeks for networking + KMS setup and approvals.

Recommendation: if you want fastest time-to-insight, start with a Hosted trial to validate quality and initial latency numbers. If retention/KMS is a hard requirement, we should schedule a VPC trial in parallel (VPC will take longer). For benchmarking sustained throughput, move to Dedicated sandbox in week 2 if you need reserved capacity.

Ownership:
- Commercial / success owner: me (Marissa Cole)
- Technical lead / infra onboarding: Dylan Brooks (cc'd)

Next steps for your team (please confirm):
- Confirm environment preference (Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC)
- Provide test dataset (sample of ~200 queries + reference outputs) and an account we can use for API keys
- Confirm legal/procurement contact (you mentioned Tom Baxter) so we can push trial SOW/POA

Attachments: poc_checklist.xlsx (trial checklist), poa_requirements.pdf (procurement items)

I'll draft a short mutual action plan once you confirm environment choice.

Best,
Marissa

Sara — great questions. Short answers and concrete ask below.

1) Latency variance:
- Hosted: typically adds a small multi-tenant variance; in our experience 95th percentile is within ~10-20% of Dedicated for short seq lengths. It is usually sufficient to validate model quality and baseline latencies.
- Dedicated: more predictable tail behavior since capacity is reserved; recommended if you need strict SLOs for throughput/latency benchmarking.

2) Data retention:
- Hosted: we can enforce a 30-day retention policy for trial data, and provide deletion logs, but if you require customer-managed keys (KMS) and strict network isolation, VPC is required.
- VPC: provides KMS/HSM integration and full control over retention and audit logs.

3) Timeline:
- If you want to start 2027-02-25 we can aim for Hosted (same-day to 48h provisioning) or Dedicated sandbox (1 week). VPC will not be ready by 02-25 due to networking/KMS lead time.

Action items (from Redwood):
- I'll prepare the trial SOW and send DocuSign link (target today)
- Dylan will provision a Hosted trial environment and share API keys once we get access list and sample data
- If you confirm Dedicated, we'll provision reserved sandbox and share ETA (~1 week)

Tom — to help Marissa move the SOW, could you confirm: 
- PO/POA format your team prefers
- Any procurement constraints (PO value limits, billing entity)

I'll attach the SOW draft (link via DocuSign) and our onboarding checklist.
